requirements.name: profile-csv-file
requirements.text:
Build a command-line tool that profiles a CSV file. For every column it infers a type and reports
row, null, and distinct counts, the minimum and maximum, and for numeric columns the sum, mean, and
median.

requirements.name: list-frequent-values
requirements.text: It also lists the most frequent values of one column.

requirements.name: go-stdlib-module
requirements.text:
Implement in Go 1.22 or newer using only the standard library. The application root is a Go
module, and its executable is the main package at `./cmd/csvstat`.

requirements.name: tests-under-go-test
requirements.text: Tests run under `go test`.

requirements.name: run-harness
requirements.text:
The harness runs `go build -o <temporary path> ./cmd/csvstat` and then runs 22 checks. Each check
compares one command's exit code and standard output with a known answer.

requirements.name: command-syntax
requirements.text: Options precede the file. Exactly one file is required.

requirements.name: column-option
requirements.text: | `--column <name>` | Profile only the named column. |

requirements.name: freq-option
requirements.text: | `--freq <name>` | List the most frequent values of the named column instead of profiling. |

requirements.name: top-option
requirements.text: | `--top <n>` | With `--freq`, list at most `<n>` values. A positive integer; default `5`. |

requirements.name: option-combinations
requirements.text: `--column` and `--freq` cannot be combined. `--top` is valid only with `--freq`.

requirements.name: csv-parsing
requirements.text:
The file is UTF-8 CSV as RFC 4180 defines it, read with Go's `encoding/csv`. The first record
is the header.

requirements.name: trim-values
requirements.text:
Every header name and every value is trimmed of leading and trailing spaces before any other
rule applies.

requirements.name: reject-bad-files
requirements.text:
The file is **rejected** when it is empty, when a header name is empty or repeated, or when any
record has a different number of fields from the header.

requirements.name: null-detection
requirements.text:
**Null.** A value is null when it is empty, or when it equals `NA`, `N/A`, or `NULL` ignoring
case. All other values are non-null.

requirements.name: date-type-inference
requirements.text: | `date` | matches `YYYY-MM-DD` and is a real calendar date (`2025-02-30` is not) |

requirements.name: boolean-text-empty-inference
requirements.text:
| `boolean` | equals `true` or `false`, ignoring case |
| `text` | anything |

A column with no non-null values has type `empty`.

requirements.name: count-fields
requirements.text:
| `rows` | Number of data records. |
| `nulls` | Number of null values. |
| `distinct` | Number of different non-null values, compared as exact strings after trimming. |

requirements.name: min-max-by-type
requirements.text: | `min`, `max` | `integer`: the smallest and largest value as an integer. `number`: as a decimal. `date`: earliest and latest. `boolean`: `false` if any value is false, else `true`; `true` if any value is true, else `false`. `text`: smallest and largest by byte value. `empty`: empty. |

requirements.name: sum-field
requirements.text: | `sum` | `integer`: the integer total. `number`: the decimal total. Otherwise empty. |

requirements.name: mean-field
requirements.text: | `mean` | `integer` and `number`: total divided by non-null count. Otherwise empty. |

requirements.name: median-field
requirements.text: | `median` | `integer` and `number`: the middle value of the sorted non-null values, or the mean of the two middle values when the count is even. Otherwise empty. |

requirements.name: decimal-formatting
requirements.text:
**Decimals.** Every `number` `min`, `max`, and `sum`, and every `mean` and `median`, is written with
exactly two decimal places, rounded half away from zero from the exact value, with a leading `-`
when negative and no thousands separator: `1012.50`, `-12.21`, `0.00`. Integer `min`, `max`, and
`sum` are written as plain integers.

requirements.name: profile-output-format
requirements.text:
Header `column,type,rows,nulls,distinct,min,max,sum,mean,median`, then one row per column in file
order (or the one named by `--column`).

requirements.name: frequency-output
requirements.text:
Header `value,count`, then one row per distinct non-null value of the column, ordered by count
descending, then value ascending by byte value, at most `--top` rows. Null values are not listed. A
column with no non-null values writes only the header.

requirements.name: csv-output-format
requirements.text:
CSV on standard output with `\n` line endings. A field that contains a comma, a double quote, or a
newline is quoted as RFC 4180 specifies; Go's `encoding/csv` writer produces this format.

requirements.name: failure-output
requirements.text:
A failing command writes nothing to standard output and one diagnostic line to standard error naming
the file and, for a rejected record, its line number.

requirements.name: exit-operational-failure
requirements.text: | `1` | Operational failure: the file cannot be opened or read. |

requirements.name: exit-usage-error
requirements.text: | `2` | Usage error: missing or extra file, unknown option, missing option value, `--top` not a positive integer, `--top` without `--freq`, `--column` with `--freq`. |

requirements.name: exit-rejected
requirements.text: | `3` | Rejected: empty file, empty or repeated header name, ragged record, or a column name that is not in the header. |

requirements.name: test-script
requirements.text:
The completed application provides a POSIX-compatible `bin/test.sh` that runs `go vet ./...` and
`go test ./...` from the application root and exits zero only when both pass. The suite covers
each type, each statistic, null handling, rounding, each output form, and each exit code using
files written by the tests.

requirements.name: header-only-input
requirements.text: sku,price,in_stock

requirements.name: reject-ragged-record
requirements.text:
sku,price,in_stock
A1,9.99,true
A2,4.50,false
A3,1.25,true,extra
A4,3.00,false

requirements.name: build-csvstat
requirements.text: Builds ./cmd/csvstat with `go build` and compares every command's exit code and standard output

requirements.name: reject-input-and-failures
requirements.text: # ── E. Rejected input and operational failures ───────────────────────────────────────────

requirements.name: pass-grader
requirements.text: Exit 0 only when the build succeeds and every check passes.
